'''Anthony F. J. Levi''' (born 1959) is a British-born engineer and academic. He is professor of electrical and computer engineering at the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering of the [[University of Southern California]] (USC). <ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=jrondon |date=2025-03-21 |title=March 21, 2025 {{!}} Why don't molecules ever stop moving? - California NanoSystems Institute |url=https://cnsi.ucla.edu/march-21-2025-faculty-in-the-news-popular-science-magazine/ |access-date=2025-04-24 |language=en-US}}</ref>

He is known for inventing ''hot electron spectroscopy'', discovering ''[[ballistic electron transport]]'' in heterostructure bipolar transistors, and demonstrating ''room-temperature unipolar ballistic transistors''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Chip Scan: 3D X-Ray Imaging of CMOS Integrated Circuits - Can you trust the electronics you use? - Anthony F.J. Levi |url=https://pswscience.org/meeting/2467/ |access-date=2025-04-24 |website=PSW Science |language=en}}</ref>

His research focuses on [[Semiconductor device|semiconductor device physics]], [[optoelectronics]], and [[hardware security]].<ref name=":1" />

== Education and career ==
He received his Ph.D. in Physics from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1983. Following his doctoral studies, he joined [[Bell Labs|AT&T Bell Laboratories]].<ref name=":0" />

At Bell Labs, he conducted research in [[semiconductor device]] technology, including the discovery of [[Ballistic conduction|ballistic electron transport]] in heterostructure [[Bipolar junction transistor|bipolar transistors]] and the demonstration of room-temperature unipolar transistors with [[Ballistic conduction|ballistic electron transport]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Levi |first=A. F. J. |url=https://store.ioppublishing.org/page/detail/Essential-Semiconductor-Laser-Device-Physics//?k=9780750329293 |title=Essential Semiconductor Laser Device Physics |date=2018-07-17 |publisher=Morgan & Claypool Publishers |isbn=978-0-7503-2929-3 |language=en}}</ref>

In 1993, Levi joined the faculty at the [[University of Southern California]], where he holds appointments in the Ming Hsieh Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering and the Department of Physics and Astronomy.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=A. F. J. Levi – Advanced Electronic and Photonic Technology |url=https://alevi.usc.edu/a-f-j-levi/ |access-date=2025-05-06 |website=alevi.usc.edu |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Researchers demonstrate 3D x-ray imaging of integrated circuits with a record 4nm resolution |url=https://viterbischool.usc.edu/news/2024/08/researchers-demonstrate-3d-x-ray-imaging-of-integrated-circuits-with-a-record-4nm-resolution/ |access-date=2025-04-24 |website=USC Viterbi {{!}} School of Engineering |language=en-US}}</ref> From 2018 to 2024, he served as Chair of the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering – Electrophysics.<ref name=":1" />

== Research ==
His early research contributed to the development of parallel [[Optical fiber|fiber-optic interconnects]], which are essential for enabling high-speed communication in computer and switching systems.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Levi |first=Barbara G. |date=September 1992 |title=What's the Shape of Things to Come in Semiconductor Lasers? |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article-abstract/45/9/17/406971/What-s-the-Shape-of-Things-to-Come-in? |journal=Physics Today |volume=45 |issue=9 |pages=17–18 |doi=10.1063/1.2809793|bibcode=1992PhT....45i..17L |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1063/1.99545 | title=Extreme nonequilibrium electron transport in heterojunction bipolar transistors | date=1988 | last1=Berthold | first1=K. | last2=Levi | first2=A. F. J. | last3=Walker | first3=J. | last4=Malik | first4=R. J. | journal=Applied Physics Letters | volume=52 | issue=26 | pages=2247–2249 | bibcode=1988ApPhL..52.2247B }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | doi=10.1017/CBO9780511691881 | title=Optimal Device Design |publisher=Cambridge University Press | date=2009 | isbn=978-0-521-11660-2 | editor-last1=Levi | editor-last2=Haas | editor-first1=A. F. J. | editor-first2=Stephan }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Frensley |first=William R. |date=January 2005 |title=Applied Quantum Mechanics |journal=Physics Today |volume=58 |issue=1 |pages=55–56 |doi=10.1063/1.1881905|doi-access=free |bibcode=2005PhT....58a..55L }}</ref><ref name=":4">{{cite book | doi=10.1017/9781009308083 | title=Applied Quantum Mechanics |publisher=Cambridge University Press | date=2023 | last1=Levi | first1=A. F. J. | isbn=978-1-009-30808-3 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.55.2071 | title=Injected-Hot-Electron Transport in GaAs | date=1985 | last1=Levi | first1=A. F. J. | last2=Hayes | first2=J. R. | last3=Platzman | first3=P. M. | last4=Wiegmann | first4=W. | journal=Physical Review Letters | volume=55 | issue=19 | pages=2071–2073 | pmid=10032002 | bibcode=1985PhRvL..55.2071L }}</ref>

He invented hot [[electron spectroscopy]], a method used to probe non-equilibrium<ref>{{cite book|last=Levi |first=A. F. J. |chapter=Non-Equilibrium Minority Carrier Transport |date=2020-09-10 |title=Essential Electron Transport for Device Physics |pages=8-1–8-24 |chapter-url=https://pubs.aip.org/books/book/35/chapter/20333968/Non-Equilibrium-Minority-Carrier-Transport |access-date=2025-05-06 |publisher=AIP Publishing |language=en |doi=10.1063/9780735421608_008 |isbn=978-0-7354-2158-5}}</ref> electron transport in semiconductor devices. <ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chiu |first1=T. H. |last2=Levi |first2=A. F. J. |date=1988-03-01 |title=Summary Abstract: Hot-electron transport in the AlSb/InAs/GaSb double heterostructure prepared by molecular-beam epitaxy |url=https://pubs.aip.org/avs/jvb/article-abstract/6/2/674/421633/Summary-Abstract-Hot-electron-transport-in-the?redirectedFrom=PDF |journal=Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology B: Microelectronics Processing and Phenomena |volume=6 |issue=2 |pages=674–675 |doi=10.1116/1.584387 |bibcode=1988JVSTB...6..674C |issn=0734-211X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

He is also credited with the creation of the microdisk laser, a compact and efficient semiconductor laser widely used in photonic research.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Levi |first=A. F. J. |chapter=Quantum Behavior in Mesoscale Lasers |date=2019 |title=2019 PhotonIcs & Electromagnetics Research Symposium - Spring (PIERS-Spring) |publisher=IEEE |pages=684–689 |doi=10.1109/PIERS-Spring46901.2019.9017832|isbn=978-1-7281-3403-1 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/0038-1101(94)90412-X |url=https://bpb-us-w1.wpmucdn.com/sites.usc.edu/dist/e/127/files/2018/05/161-1j9m4ah.pdf |title=Microdisk lasers |date=1994 |last1=Levi |first1=A.F.J. |journal=Solid-State Electronics |volume=37 |issue=4–6 |pages=1297–1302 |bibcode=1994SSEle..37.1297L }}</ref>

Working with [[Agilent Technologies]], Levi co-developed an [[optical connector]] plug-in package capable of transmitting data at an aggregate rate of 10&nbsp;Gb/s in late 2000.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Savage |first=Neil |date=August 1, 2002 |title=Linking With Light |work=IEEE Spectrum |url=https://spectrum.ieee.org/linking-with-light}}</ref> 

Working with the [[Paul Scherrer Institute]] and researchers at the [[USC Viterbi School of Engineering]], Levi helped advance a technique for defect detection in manufactured semiconductor chips as well as for [[reverse engineering]] of circuits.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 8, 2019 |title=Groundbreaking Method Detects Defective Computer Chips |work=USC Viterbi News |url=https://viterbischool.usc.edu/news/2019/10/groundbreaking-method-detects-defective-computer-chips/}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=October 11, 2019 |title=Technique Could Check Integrity of Computer Chips and Detect Tampering |work=Technology Networks |url=https://www.technologynetworks.com/applied-sciences/news/technique-could-check-integrity-of-computer-chips-and-detect-tampering-325079}}</ref>

In an interview with [[Reuters]], Levi commented on [[supply chain]] concerns facing the chip industry in the U.S. during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], suggesting that such issues could be mitigated by focusing on rebuilding the U.S. chip manufacturing and packaging industry.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Nellis |first1=Stephen |last2=Jin |first2=Hyunjoo |date=April 13, 2021 |title=Focus: Biden's chip dreams face reality check of supply chain complexity |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/bidens-chip-dreams-face-reality-check-supply-chain-complexity-2021-04-13/}}</ref>

Levi’s research combines experimental and theoretical approaches across multiple domains, reflecting a broad and integrative vision that bridges [[solid-state physics]], [[quantum electronics]], and [[Applied engineering (field)|applied engineering]].<ref name=":3" /> 

His pioneering work in semiconductor device physics and optoelectronics includes studies on nonequilibrium electron transport, ballistic electron transport in transistors, and microdisk lasers, which have advanced the understanding of high-speed electronic and photonic systems. <ref name=":2" />

In the field of [[photonics]] and [[quantum engineering]], Levi has developed integrated photonic systems and explored the quantum-classical boundaries in device design, contributing to innovations in both optical communication and quantum information processing.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Chip Scan: 3D X-Ray Imaging of CMOS Integrated Circuits - Can you trust the electronics you use? - Anthony F.J. Levi |url=https://pswscience.org/meeting/2467/ |access-date=2025-11-21 |website=PSW Science |language=en}}</ref> 

He has also demonstrated leadership in hardware security and chip imaging, particularly through the development of 3D X-ray imaging technologies used for microchip inspection and tamper detection, a research area that has received significant attention in the scientific and technical press since 2019.<ref name=":5" /> 

Levi has led several notable projects at USC in collaboration with industry and government partners. Among these, the 3D X-ray microchip imaging focuses on developing high-resolution 3D X-ray techniques for [[integrated circuit]] inspection, enabling the detection of structural defects and unauthorized modifications in semiconductor devices.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Institute |first=Paul Scherrer |last2=Senn |first2=Benjamin A. |date=2024-05-08 |title=X-ray world record: Looking inside a microchip with 4 nm precision |url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/x-ray-world-record-looking-inside-a-microchip-wi-4/ |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Aidukas |first=Tomas |last2=Phillips |first2=Nicholas W. |last3=Diaz |first3=Ana |last4=Poghosyan |first4=Emiliya |last5=Müller |first5=Elisabeth |last6=Levi |first6=A. F. J. |last7=Aeppli |first7=Gabriel |last8=Guizar-Sicairos |first8=Manuel |last9=Holler |first9=Mirko |date=2024-08-01 |title=High-performance 4-nm-resolution X-ray tomography using burst ptychography |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07615-6 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=632 |issue=8023 |pages=81–88 |doi=10.1038/s41586-024-07615-6 |issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Another key initiative, quantum and hybrid device optimization, involves ongoing studies on the design, performance limits, and control of hybrid classical–quantum devices, integrating concepts from applied quantum mechanics and nanofabrication. 

Levi is the author of several widely used textbooks that connect fundamental physics with practical device design. His book ''Applied Quantum Mechanics'' is a comprehensive, application-focused text written for engineers, materials scientists, and applied physicists.<ref name=":4" /> Now in its third edition, this book emphasizes real-world examples and includes worked problems, as well as coverage of quantum engineering, quantum information processing, and device optimization. ''Essential Semiconductor Laser Device Physics'', now in its second edition, offers a concise overview of semiconductor laser principles, threshold behavior, and design strategies, serving as a key reference for engineers and researchers working on semiconductor lasers.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Levi |first=A. F. J. |title=Essential semiconductor laser device physics |date=2018 |publisher=Morgan & Claypool Publishers |isbn=978-1-64327-029-6 |edition=Version: 20180701 |series=IOP concise physics |location=San Rafael, CA, USA}}</ref> ''Essential Classical Mechanics for Device Physics'' is a concise introduction to classical mechanics concepts, providing readers with the theoretical and mathematical foundation for modern device design.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Levi |first=A. F. J. |title=Essential classical mechanics for device physics |date=2016 |publisher=Morgan & Claypool Publishers |isbn=978-1-68174-412-4 |edition=Version: 20160901 |series=IOP concise physics |location=San Rafael, CA}}</ref>
